reviews.one_line_contribution: The claim is that a retrieved memory block imprints its action/tool histogram onto an agent's action prior largely independently of the current state, and that because retrieval changes the block at every step, removing that component requires a per-retrieval probe-estimated logit offset (MAC) rather than a scalar context downweight (CFG/CAD) or a single bank-wide base-rate offset; the deliverable is a double dissociation on ALFWorld plus a causally controlled measurement of the imprinting effect.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Zhao et al. 2021 (Calibrate Before Use) is the threat the proposal underestimates, and not for the reason it concedes. Its content-free probe is defined *per prompt*: the probe is run with the demonstration set that is actually in context. That the demonstration set happens to be fixed across a classification benchmark is a property of the benchmark, not of the method. Under retrieval, running the same probe per query is the method as originally specified, not an extension of it, so the 'adaptivity dissociation' (P4) is a comparison against a degenerate simplification the authors introduced themselves; no calibration paper ever proposed the global bank offset. Two further items bite. (a) Zheng et al., ICLR 2024, 'Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors' / PriDe already estimates a query-independent prior over an enumerable choice set and subtracts it at inference with an instance-level, cheaply amortised estimate - structurally the same object as MAC over an enumerable action set, and it already prices estimate-once-vs-estimate-per-instance. (b) Fei et al. 2023 Domain-Context Calibration is essentially the 'real-state-averaged estimator' of E2c, so the proposal's own fallback estimator is prior art. Separately, Sanchez et al. 2023 explicitly support negative/alternative contrast prompts, which makes MAC a member of the contrastive-logit-adjustment family (subtract lambda times log p(a | block, null query)) rather than a different instrument from CFG/CAD (subtract gamma times log p(a | no block, query)). Both are one scalar times one log-ratio vector; the 'factorisation vs scaling' dichotomy in the Short Hypothesis is a rhetorical contrast between two choices of anchor prompt, not between two classes of correction.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline effect sizes are unanchored to any estimate of available headroom, and by the proposal's own arithmetic the accept-case branch is the unlikely one. The pilot that motivates the work reports memory fixing zero items and breaking six to seven, and reports that simply cutting k already neutralises that harm. On 1,000 ALFWorld games the total damage MAC can undo is bounded by the uncalibrated-vs-no-memory gap, which nothing in E0 is required to measure before the confirmatory run commits: E0's gate only asks that injection move success 'in either direction' beyond the noise floor. If that gap is, say, 2-3 points, then P3 (MAC beats best-tuned CFG by >=4 points episode success) and P4 (MAC beats the global offset by >=4 points) are arithmetically close to unreachable unless CFG at gamma* is actively worse than doing nothing, and conditions (ii)-(v) of E5 will all land inside the 3.0-point McNemar MDE. The pre-commitments then fire: P3 parity reduces the paper to 'the channels are not separable in practice', P4 parity reduces it to 'classic contextual calibration transfers unchanged to agents'. Those are the modal outcomes, not the tail. Compounding this, gamma* and lambda* are selected on a 200-game validation split whose own MDE is roughly 6-7 points - larger than every difference the screening must resolve - so 'best-tuned CFG' is a noise draw, and the headline MAC-vs-CFG contrast inherits a selection bias in MAC's favour that no amount of held-out discipline in E5 repairs. A second, independent objection an AC will raise: E2(a) validates the probe by showing its estimate tracks the *designed* block share (rho >= 0.7), i.e. the probe is approximately a monotone function of the literal action histogram, and ablation (e) prices exactly that free zero-forward-pass estimator - yet (e) is an ablation, not a confirmatory arm. If (e) ties, the entire probe apparatus and the P0 gate are decorative and MAC collapses to 'subtract lambda times the log frequency of each verb in the injected block', which is a two-line heuristic and a sibling of the action-balanced-retrieval baseline in logit space. A third: E1's substitution design changes *which* memory items are present in order to change the share of verb v, matched only on mean retrieval score and token count. Mean retrieval score is not relevance, and Risk 6 concedes the substitution pool exists only for some states, so the effect is measured on a state subset selected by pool availability and correlated with how stereotyped the state's action distribution already is - a confound the mixed-effects correctness fixed effect does not absorb.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Run the literature search before submitting anything rather than pre-committing to run it; it has now failed twice and a third silent round is not a tooling excuse an AC can accept. 2) Make E0 measure and report the uncalibrated-vs-no-memory headroom on the 200-game validation split, then re-derive P3/P4 thresholds from it and publish a stop rule: if the headroom is below roughly 2x the confirmatory MDE, the confirmatory grid cannot support the double dissociation and should be replaced by the step-level test as primary. The step-level outcome (30,000 paired steps, MDE 0.9) is already the higher-powered instrument and should be the pre-registered primary, with episode success secondary. 3) Select gamma and lambda on the step-level metric, or enlarge the validation split, so hyperparameter selection is not noise. 4) Write down MAC's decode rule explicitly and add negative-prompt CFG - contrast prompt = injected block with a nulled goal - as its own arm in E5. If that arm equals MAC, say so and reframe the contribution as 'which contrast prompt should agentic calibration use', which is a smaller but defensible and still useful claim. 5) Promote ablation (e), the literal-histogram zero-forward-pass calibrator, into the confirmatory grid; it is the true competitor. 6) Add an adaptivity-matched, decode-free baseline (below) so P4 tests adaptivity rather than MAC's machinery. 7) Report imprinting on the states *without* an equal-relevance substitution pool via a weaker design, or bound the selection effect, so E1 is not silently restricted to a convenient subset.
reviews.missing_baseline: A per-retrieval adaptive injection budget: gate or trim the block at each step on the JSD between its verb histogram and the bank marginal, a quantity E0 already computes for free with no forward pass and no decode-time correction. As written, P4 contrasts a per-retrieval method (MAC) with a fixed offset and calls the difference 'adaptivity', but the only adaptive arm in the grid is also the only arm with a probe and a logit correction, so adaptivity is perfectly confounded with mechanism. If adaptive-k matches MAC, the novelty-bearing prediction is answered against the proposal and the paper reduces to the pilot's own volume lever made per-step. Also absent: MAC stacked on the k=2 volume reduction (the pilot-validated neutraliser - showing MAC adds nothing on top of k=2 would be decisive), the negative-prompt CFG arm described above, and any pre-registered MAC-vs-no-memory net-gain test - none of P3-P5 requires calibrated memory to beat having no memory at all, which is the comparison a reader actually cares about.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is a self-declared failure for the second consecutive round: zero queries returned, no verified closest work, no verified gap. The honesty is genuine and unusual, and the graceful-degradation scenarios (a)-(c) are well constructed, but honesty about an unsearched claim does not convert it into a neutral - novelty here is simply not established, and scenario (c) in the authors' own list ('a preprint already establishes per-retrieval calibration under RAG-style variable demonstrations') is the one I would bet on, because kNN/retrieval-based ICL with per-query demonstration sets has been standard since 2022 and calibrating it is the first thing anyone tries. I cannot verify 2025-2026 arXiv from here either, but the burden is the authors'. Beyond that, the check omits indexed work it should already know without any search: Zheng et al. ICLR 2024 (PriDe) on estimating and removing a query-independent prior over an enumerable choice set, the substantial selection- and frequency-bias literature on LLM function/tool calling, and the fact that Fei et al. 2023's domain-context calibration is the proposal's own E2c fallback estimator. A collision check that misses prior work reachable from the Related Work section's own citation graph is thin independently of the tooling outage.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A causal, action-mix-controlled measurement that a retrieved memory block imprints its action histogram onto a sequential agent's policy largely independently of the current state, plus MAC — a per-retrieval subtraction of that query-independent component — claimed to beat both scalar context scaling (CFG/CAD) and a fixed bank-wide base-rate offset.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Zhao et al. 2021 (Calibrate Before Use), and it threatens the proposal more than the proposal admits. CC's content-free probe is computed WITH the demonstrations in the prompt, i.e. p(y | 'N/A', demos): if the demonstration block changes per query, CC's estimate changes per query automatically. MAC, as described in E2/E3 (content-free goal + templated observation + the same injected block), is literally CC recomputed per retrieval. The claim in Related Work that 'no prior calibration paper has had to answer whether adaptivity buys anything' is therefore backwards — CC was always per-context; the static-demonstration setting merely made the per-context estimate constant. The 'global bank base-rate offset' that P4 is defined against is not 'what classic ICL calibration reduces to'; it is a weaker estimator the calibration literature never proposed. Generative Calibration (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023 Findings), which estimates the label marginal by Monte-Carlo sampling under the actual prompt, and Batch Calibration (Zhou et al. 2023), which estimates the shift from the actual inputs, are both per-context estimators as well. On the decoding side, PMI/surface-form-competition scoring (Holtzman et al. 2021) and noisy-channel prompting (Min et al. 2022) are the same instrument — divide out the action's unconditional propensity under the context. What survives as genuinely new is the sequential-agent transfer plus the E1-E3 measurement, not the estimator and not the adaptivity.
reviews.strongest_objection: P4 — explicitly named as 'the second confirmatory test and the novelty-bearing one' — is a comparison against a strawman. Beating a fixed bank-wide log-marginal offset by 4 points does not establish that per-retrieval calibration is a new contribution; it establishes that a per-query estimator beats an estimator nobody proposed, while the literal 2021 method (CC with the current block in the probe prompt) IS MAC. If P4 wins, the paper's own pre-commitment ('classic contextual calibration transfers unchanged to agent memory') is the honest headline whether P4 wins or loses, which means the headline test cannot discriminate. Second, and nearly as damaging: the Short Hypothesis asserts imprinting is 'the dominant source of memory-induced breakage', but no experiment tests dominance. All four E1 arms (LOW/MID/HIGH/IRR-HIGH) are matched within 5% on token count, deliberately holding constant the one lever the pilot actually proved causal (k=7 to k=3 eliminated the harm from the same bank). There is no share x volume factorial anywhere, and the k=2 arm — the pilot's own validated neutraliser — enters E5 only conditionally, on a 500-game subset whose MDE (~4.2 pts) equals the effect size MAC is predicted to produce. So the plan can show that action share has an effect while leaving 'imprinting rather than volume explains the pilot harm' entirely untested. Third, IRR-HIGH is a weak boundary control in ALFWorld: bottom-decile-retrieval items are still ALFWorld trajectories with the same verb vocabulary ('go to', 'take', 'open'), so 'topically irrelevant' and 'action-mix matched' are nearly collinear and P1's <25%/>=50% thresholds may be unfalsifiable in practice.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Drop the strawman framing: put literal per-query Contextual Calibration in as the named baseline, concede MAC = CC-per-retrieval, and make the contribution the measurement (E1-E3 factorisation R², drift, stratified fix/break) plus the head-to-head against CFG and against the zero-forward-pass literal-histogram estimator of ablation (e). If the free histogram estimator ties the probe — a live possibility given E0 already computes the block histogram — there is no method left and the paper should be planned as a measurement paper from the start. (2) Add a share x injection-volume factorial in E1 (2 shares x 2 k values, token count varied not fixed) and put k=2 in the full 1,000-game confirmatory grid, so the 'dominant source' claim becomes testable rather than assumed. (3) Fix the tuning asymmetry: the claim that sweeping gamma over 5 values against lambda's 3 'favours the competitor' is backwards — selection on a 200-game split (MDE ~6-7 pts) is mostly selecting noise, and more grid points means more winner's-curse and worse held-out transfer for CFG. Use the same grid size for both, or select via the E6 null distribution. (4) P5 is currently untestable as written: instruction debiasing, action-balanced retrieval and GEPA-selected demonstrations are never all run on the 1,000-game held-out set (only the screening winner is, and GEPA only appears single-turn). Either carry all three into E5 or restate P5 at the power it actually has. (5) E8/P8 rests on three GEPA runs, one per condition, with no seed replication — the track's own pilot showed a null replicate reproducing the best treatment's apparent gain; run >=3 seeds per condition or drop the quantitative >=2.5-point claim. (6) Resolve the internal contradiction between Risk 11 (probe cost 'amortised across steps using that block') and E0/P4 (the block drifts step to step): if adaptivity is necessary, amortisation is not available, and the cost table must include one extra forward pass per decision step. (7) Run the pre-committed searches before, not after, writing the novelty claim.
reviews.missing_baseline: Volume reduction (k=2) at full power in the confirmatory grid. It is the pilot's own validated neutraliser and the direct rival explanation for the harm MAC claims to remove, yet E5 admits it only as a conditional sixth condition on 500 games if it happens to win screening. A reviewer will demand MAC vs k=2 at n=1,000 paired, because 'MAC produces gain where k=2 only removes harm' is a claim the plan asserts (Baselines item 6) without powering. Secondary omissions: MAC+CFG combined (needed to show the channels are complementary rather than substitutable, which is what the factorisation claim actually implies), and a plain PMI-style baseline that divides by p(a | block) with no content-free template at all, which would price the entire probe apparatus against a one-line scoring change.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is a declared null: zero searches returned results, for the second consecutive round, on a tooling failure. The proposal is commendably honest about this and refuses to read silence as novelty — but under the standard applied here that leaves novelty unestablished rather than neutral, and it is a weakness, not a wash. The three risks it flags (frequency/majority bias in LLM function-calling; calibrated or contrastive decoding on agentic memory; retrieval-induced action drift in memory-augmented agents) are exactly the low-hanging 2025-2026 extensions of Calibrate Before Use, and I share the proposal's own assessment that at least one probably exists; I cannot verify which, having not searched. What can be said from indexed work alone is that the adaptivity premise is already weakened: CC's probe is per-context by construction, and Generative Calibration and Batch Calibration both estimate the shift from the live prompt/inputs, so 'per-retrieval estimation is an open question classic calibration could not pose' does not survive contact with 2021-2023 papers, let alone 2026 preprints. Note also that the proposal's own fallback (c) — 'if a preprint already establishes per-retrieval calibration under RAG-style variable demonstrations, the novelty claim collapses to the agentic/sequential transfer' — is already the accurate description of the submission as written.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That retrieved agent memory injects a query-independent action prior — the block's action histogram copied onto the policy irrespective of state — and that removing it requires a per-retrieval probe estimate (MAC), which the paper claims will beat both scalar context scaling (CFG/CAD) and a fixed bank-level base-rate offset on ALFWorld.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Zhao et al. 2021 (Calibrate Before Use) plus the calibration successors the proposal already cites — and it concedes the mechanism. The residual novelty rests entirely on the assertion in Related Work that 'in classic ICL the demonstration set is fixed across the evaluation, so a single global offset suffices, and no prior calibration paper has had to answer whether adaptivity buys anything.' That assertion is the weakest sentence in the submission and I do not accept it. Retrieval-based ICL (Liu et al. 2022 KATE; Rubin et al. 2022 EPR) has had per-query-varying demonstration sets since 2022, and Zhao's probe is defined *relative to the current prompt* — recomputing it when the prompt changes per query is a re-run of the same equation, not a new estimator. Batch Calibration (Zhou et al. 2023) already estimates the bias adaptively at inference from the current batch rather than from a fixed global offset, and Domain-Context Calibration (Fei et al. 2023) already re-estimates it from in-domain content rather than a static content-free string. So the 'global bank base-rate offset' in E5(v) is not what the calibration literature actually prescribes under retrieval; it is a degraded variant the proposal has constructed to lose. If MAC beats it (P4), the finding is 'the textbook application of a 2021 method beats a variant nobody proposed'; if it ties, the proposal pre-commits to the title 'classic contextual calibration transfers unchanged'. Both branches of the novelty-bearing prediction land below an ICLR main-track bar.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory design has no established dynamic range, so P3 and P4 are close to arithmetically unwinnable. Every arm in E5 — MAC, CFG@γ*, the global offset, k=2, instruction debiasing — is a correction applied to the *same* uncalibrated k=4 injection, so the spread between any two of them is bounded above by the total effect of that injection relative to no-memory. The proposal never bounds that quantity: E0's gate only asks that injection 'moves ALFWorld success beyond the measured noise floor in either direction,' i.e. it can pass at ~3-4 points, and the antecedent pilot it leans on reports memory breaking six to seven items in absolute counts, not a large percentage swing. If uncalibrated injection costs, say, 3 points, then no two corrections can differ by the ≥4 points P3 and P4 demand, and both headline predictions fail for reasons that have nothing to do with whether the factorisation is real. The paper then reports 'parity' three times and concludes something it did not test. Second, the rescue from this is invalid as written: the 'pre-registered secondary, higher-power outcome' of ~30,000 *paired* decision steps with MDE ≈ 0.9 does not exist. Conditions share an initial state, but the moment MAC and CFG select different actions the episodes occupy different environment states, and every subsequent step is unpaired. McNemar on step-level executed-action correctness across 30 steps × 1,000 games is therefore not a paired test after the first divergence; the genuinely paired sample is the first divergent step plus whatever re-converges by luck, which is far smaller and non-randomly selected (episodes that never diverge contribute all their steps and zero signal, inflating concordance and deflating the apparent MDE). Third, no prediction requires MAC to beat the no-memory floor. E5 includes condition (i), but P3-P5 only pit MAC against other memory-using arms, so the paper can declare a double dissociation while every memory condition sits below no-memory — which is exactly what the pilot (zero fixes, six-to-seven breaks) predicts.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Make E0 a quantitative gate, not a directional one: measure |uncalibrated k=4 − no-memory| on the 200-game validation split first, and re-derive the P3/P4 thresholds as a stated fraction of that measured range rather than fixing them at ≥4 points a priori; if the range is under ~6 points, the confirmatory grid as designed cannot separate the arms and should be redesigned (e.g. larger k, or a domain where injection does more damage) before the 5,500 episodes are spent. (2) Add MAC > no-memory as a pre-registered gating contrast ahead of P3/P4 — without it, 'calibrated memory' can win the dissociation while losing to using no memory at all. (3) Drop the claim of 30,000 paired steps; replace it with the analysis the proposal already knows how to do — teacher-forced scoring of both conditions on *identical* held-out states (the E1 machinery) — plus a first-divergence-anchored outcome (does the first differing action agree with the expert plan) that is honestly paired at n = number of divergent episodes. (4) Replace the 'global bank base-rate offset' with the strong form of the static competitor: Zhao's content-free probe computed once on a *fixed* injected block, so that the comparison is adaptivity-vs-nonadaptivity at matched estimator quality rather than probe-vs-marginal. (5) Run the eight pre-committed queries before submission; a third failed search should postpone the paper, not be disclosed and proceeded past.
reviews.missing_baseline: A fixed-block memory arm: the same, non-retrieved injected block (matched token count and bank-representative action mix) used for every query and every step. This is the actual control for the entire adaptivity claim — it is the condition under which a single global correction is provably sufficient, and comparing it against retrieved k=4 is what establishes that per-query histogram variation costs anything in the first place. Without it, E0's JSD/drift statistics are descriptive only and P4 tests estimator quality rather than adaptivity. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also demand: an oracle/upper-bound arm (subtract the *true* per-block action marginal computed by averaging over held-out real states, i.e. E2c's estimator used as the correction rather than only as a validity check) to bound how much of the harm any calibration can recover; and MAC applied on top of k=2 volume reduction, since the pilot already showed k=2 neutralises the harm and the paper never tests whether MAC adds anything to the cheap fix it must beat.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin — it is empty, and by the proposal's own admission for the second consecutive round: zero results returned, tool failure, 'no verified closest recent work and no verified gap.' The proposal deserves credit for saying so plainly rather than dressing up silence as novelty, and for enumerating exact future queries and graceful-degradation branches (a)/(b)/(c). But an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness, and here it compounds with a conceded four-year-old mechanism: the entire remaining contribution sits in the two areas the proposal itself lists as 'materially likely' collisions — frequency/majority bias in LLM tool selection, and calibrated/contrastive decoding applied to agentic memory. It also flags branch (c), per-retrieval calibration under RAG-style variable demonstrations, under which 'the novelty claim collapses to the agentic/sequential transfer.' I judge branch (c) as already partly realised by indexed work rather than a hypothetical preprint risk: retrieval-conditioned demonstration selection plus contextual calibration is a documented combination, and Batch Calibration is an explicitly inference-time-adaptive bias estimate. So the collision risk is not merely unverified, it is unverified on top of an indexed threat the proposal mischaracterises. I cannot name a specific 2025-2026 arXiv preprint from within the constraints of this review, and I will not invent one — but the burden is the authors', and after two failed searches it remains entirely unmet.
